name: Norilsk Nickel

summary.text: Norilsk Nickel is a Russian metals producer. In November 1995 a 38 percent stake was auctioned under the loans-for-shares programme in an auction run by Oneximbank; the winning bid, by Vladimir Potanin's Interros group, was about $170.1 million, and the government's loan was never repaid, so Oneximbank kept the collateral shares. Analysts criticised the sale as an insider deal.

sources.title: Daniel Treisman, 'Loans for Shares' Revisited (NBER Working Paper 15819)

facts.claim: Analysts criticised the sale of 38 percent of Norilsk Nickel in the 1995 loans-for-shares auction as an insider deal fixed in favour of Oneximbank.
facts.quote: Analysts later criticized the sale of 38 percent of Norilsk Nickel as an insider deal fixed in favor of Oneximbank.

facts.claim: The government's loans under the scheme were never repaid, so Oneximbank received ownership of the collateral shares in the privatised enterprises.
facts.quote: The government's loans were never repaid, so Onexim received ownership of the collateral, which was the shares in the privatized enterprises.

facts.claim: Treisman's NBER paper argues the scheme's execution appeared corrupt but that pricing was in most cases in line with international practice.
facts.quote: the pricing in most cases was in line with international practice

sources.title: Daniel Treisman, 'Loans for Shares' Revisited (NBER Working Paper 15819)

openQuestions: Site claim tested: Norilsk Nickel's acquisition for a low price via loans-for-shares is supported ($170.1 million for 38 percent, per a non-academic profile that also claims a $355 million rival bid was disqualified; not cross-checked). The Yeltsin campaign-funding quid pro quo was not confirmed.
